lem-2.2.i.statement: For every input y and (i,s) in [m] x {0,1}^r: i wins at s iff all K_{k,m} tests pass, namely (a) X_i[b]=1 for each b; (b) for each j != i, X_j[p_{i,s,j}]=0; (c) for each h and each non-input gate, the claimed value equals the gate function of its predecessors, read from the transcript or from A_{i,h}; (d) for each h, claimed d=1 and claimed b=s_h. Each test is computed by a deterministic adaptive bit-query decision tree of depth at most max(3,l+1), which is l+1 for m>=4: a pointer test reads l pointer bits, then the one target bit they select, while gate tests read at most three fixed bits. A pointer test is not a function of a small fixed set of bits: it can depend on all l+m pointer and target coordinates.
lem-2.2.i.first_lean_target: theorem winsAt_iff_tests (y i s) : WinsAt y i s <-> forall e : TestIdx cfg, test y i s e = true; and def testTree (e) : DTree with depth <= max 3 (l+1) and testTree.eval y = test y i s e. State no support bound.
lem-2.2.i.proof_notes: Induction in topological order: all gate tests pass iff transcript equals true evaluation. Uses the correctness half of lem-2.1.iii for the meaning of (d), not its size bound. Corrected from 'function of O(log m) input bits' (r1, r2, r3).

def-deg.statement: deg(f) is the degree of the unique real multilinear polynomial agreeing with f on the cube, with degree 0 for every constant function, including the zero function. With this convention it is unchanged by replacing input or output bits by signs.

eq-5.first_lean_target: def Lval (k t) : Nat := Nat.floor (m^(1-1/k) / (logb 2 m)^2).
eq-5.proof_notes: Definition only. The inequality displayed in Eq. 5 is lem-2.1.i.

lem-2.1.i.first_lean_target: Named hypothesis BansalSinha k := forall^f t, Lval k t < R (Forr k t). Do not prove. Optionally state BansalSinhaCor14 := exists c>0, for each k>=2, for all large n (threshold depending on k), c/k^29*(2^n/log(k 2^n))^(1-1/k) <= R (forr k n), and derive BansalSinha.
lem-2.1.i.proof_notes: Checked against arXiv:2008.07003v3 Eqs. 1.1-1.3, Theorem 1.3, Corollary 1.4 (p.4): normalisation, delta=2^{-5k}, delta/2 threshold, depth, error 1/3 on valid inputs all match. Statement match only; their proof was not rechecked. Their proof needs 'large enough N' (Section 5.4, p.38), so the threshold depends on k. Pin v3. Funnel adjudication (F-BS-54): the last displayed inequality of Section 5.4 fails for levels l>k when k>=3, leaving an unbounded factor log(kN)^((l/k-1)/2); as displayed, the argument gives the weaker denominator log(kN)^(1-1/(k(k-1))). Either form exceeds L for fixed k, and the Lean development proves this row directly without the citation.

claim-bs-to-L.statement: For fixed k>=2 and the positive constant c of the Bansal-Sinha bound: for all sufficiently large powers of four m, c k^{-29} (m/log(km))^{1-1/k} > floor(m^{1-1/k}/(log_2 m)^2).
claim-bs-to-L.proof_notes: Funnel adjudication (F-BS-TIE, F-BS-C): k>=2 and c>0 made explicit; the comparison is false for c=0. No Lean declaration states this comparison; QuarticQuery.ForrelationLower.bansalSinhaLower proves the consequence L<R(P) directly and is tied to lem-2.1.i only.

eq-17.first_lean_target: def Gval (m L) : Nat := m * L / 100.
eq-17.proof_notes: Definition only. The inequality displayed in Eq. 17 is prop-4.2.

claim-minimax-mu.statement: If L<R(P), there is a distribution mu on dom P, which is in particular nonempty, such that every deterministic tree of depth <=L has success probability <=2/3 under mu.
claim-minimax-mu.first_lean_target: theorem yao_hard_dist (P) (L) (h : L < R P) : exists mu : PMF P.dom, forall T : DTree n L, mu.prob (T.eval = P) <= 2/3.
claim-minimax-mu.proof_notes: Generic finite minimax over promised inputs. The value is <2/3, the paper records <=2/3 afterwards. Does not use Lemma 4.1 or Lemma 2.1(i). An empty domain gives R=0, so it contradicts the hypothesis.

claim-address-guess.statement: Under mu from claim-minimax-mu, for U_1,...,U_r iid mu, every classical algorithm making at most L queries to each U_h, given information independent of (U_1,...,U_r), outputs (P(U_1),...,P(U_r)) with probability <=(2/3)^r.
claim-address-guess.first_lean_target: theorem address_guess_le (P L mu hmu) : direct corollary of capped_direct_product with beta=2/3.
claim-address-guess.proof_notes: Second half of the old claim-minimax-mu.

prop-4.2-generic.statement: Let m=4^t with t>=1 and r=40t. Let P be a partial function on km bits with an exact circuit C (d=1 iff defined, and d=1 implies b=P), and F the total function built from (P,C). If 1<=L<=m and L<R(P), then R(F)>floor(mL/100).
prop-4.2-generic.first_lean_target: theorem R_F_gt (cfg) (hL1 : 1 <= L) (hLm : L <= m) (hP : L < R P) : Gval m L < R (F cfg).
prop-4.2-generic.proof_notes: Non-asymptotic. Circuit size and the quantum decoder are absent. Needs the read-all witness for R(F).

prop-4.2.first_lean_target: Instance of R_F_gt with the efficient forrCircuit, hP from BansalSinha k, and 1<=L<=m eventually in t.
prop-4.2.proof_notes: Concrete corollary. It must use the same circuit as prop-3.3.

claim-tail.proof_notes: Paper's exponent is 2-11.699=-9.699. With L<=m, G<=m^2/100. Either 3^20>2^31 gives (2/3)^(40t)<m^-11 and the target m^-9, or the shorter 4/9<=1/2 gives <=m^-10 and (1/100) m^-8; each suffices. Uniform in t>=1, no limit needed.

cor-cubic-refuted.statement: It is false that R(f) = O(Q(f)^3) for all total Boolean f ([3, Conjecture 2]): no C satisfies R(f) <= C Q(f)^3 for all total f.
external_inputs: [3] ABKRT arXiv:2010.12629v1 Conjecture 2, p.20 (checked); ABKRT p.1 says it subsumes arXiv:2004.13231, whose text was not held
cor-cubic-refuted.proof_notes: k=3 suffices: R >= Q^{10/3 - o(1)}. From R<=C Q^3 get R<=C(1+Q)^3 and contradict claim-exponent-ratio at alpha=3; Q>=1 is not needed. k=2 gives only exponent 3 up to logs.

def-log-convention.first_lean_target: Use Nat.clog 2 (1000*m) for T, rval t := 40*t for r, lval t := 2*t for l, and Real.logb 2 for L.

eq-2.proof_notes: Asymptotic packaging of prop-3.3 and prop-4.2; no new mathematics. b_k may be taken as 4 for every k (the k-dependence sits in C_k).

eq-8.statement: Outward pointer condition at address s: X_j[p_{i,s,j}] = 0 for every j != i. Eq. 8 of the paper is the case s=s_i.
eq-8.proof_notes: Orientation is the crux of the construction: only a true winner defeats every rival. GPW [15] Section 2.1 already has a pointer chain through one zero per rival; the direct, hard-addressed per-rival pointers are what is specific here.

def-win-at-address.statement: WinsAt(y,i,s) holds iff X_i=1^m, for every h the transcript in B_{i,s} on A_{i,h} is correct with outputs d=1 and b=s_h, and eq-8 holds at s. The paper's wording, i is a winner and s=s_i, is equivalent by claim-winner-fidelity.

def-winner.proof_notes: Lean: IsWinner y i := exists s, WinsAt y i s. This agrees with the paper's definition only through claim-winner-fidelity.

claim-winner-fidelity.statement: Given the correctness half of lem-2.1.iii: WinsAt(y,i,s) iff X_i=1^m, every P(A_{i,h}) is defined, s=s_i, the transcripts in B_{i,s} are correct, and eq-8 holds. Hence exists s, WinsAt(y,i,s) is the paper's winner condition.
claim-winner-fidelity.first_lean_target: theorem winsAt_iff_paper (hC : CircuitSpec C P) : WinsAt y i s <-> PaperWinner y i s.

lem-3.1.statement: For 0<gamma<=1/2 and 0<eta<1/2 there is a single procedure, black-box in A and A^{-1} and with call counts depending only on gamma and eta, using O(gamma^{-1/2} log(1/eta)) calls for every p and on every branch, such that for every state preparation A with a success bit, success probability p and, if p>0, normalized successful state |g>: it reports failure or produces a successful outcome; conditional on success the output is |g> up to global phase; if p>=gamma, failure probability <=eta; if p=0 it always reports failure.
lem-3.1.first_lean_target: def amplify (gamma eta) (A : oracle-access to a preparation) : program, whose structure does not inspect A; theorem amplify_spec: calls <= C*gamma^(-1/2)*log(1/eta), (gamma <= p -> failProb <= eta), (p = 0 -> failProb = 1), and output state on success is projectively g.

prop-3.2.proof_notes: The paper's 'Fix an input' (line 354) concerns the analysis only: the algorithm is chosen before x, from the comparison circuit alone. Only complementarity and exact sampling are used. Split into the classical ideal part (Stage 1) and the quantum sampling part (Stage 5).

def-R.proof_notes: Paper says 'minimum worst-case numbers of bit queries'. Worst-case randomized cost equals a mixture of depth-q trees (line 576-577). Set the definition as a mixture so that minimax applies directly. Prove a read-all witness: concluding G<R f from a sInf needs the feasible set nonempty.

def-Q.proof_notes: The paper never gives a formal model. The upper bound uses intermediate measurement, classical control and fresh registers; lem-A.2 purifies to a fixed sequence. The single definition must serve both directions. Algorithms are chosen before x. A read-all witness makes the sInf meaningful. See doubt D2.

[19] Midrijanis quant-ph/0403168v2, inside the proof of Theorem 4, p.4, using Lemma 3 on maxonomials (checked; Theorem 4 itself states D<=2deg^3). Proof in the paper

thm-1.1.proof_notes: Reader audit: 4 lies in the set by thm-A.1; every alpha in [0,4) is excluded by claim-no-smaller-exponent; no upward closure needed. Evidence class of alphaTot_eq_four is conditional on BansalSinha k for all k>=2, and it must be labelled so. Two readings are not a verification.

external_inputs: [12] BHMT Lemma 1 and Eq. 8, pp.5-7 (checked); [11] Boyer et al. (rotation fact, proved in the paper)

def-column-layout.proof_notes: Input length n = m(m + r k m + 2^r((m-1) l + r S)) with 2^r=m^20, hence n=O_k(m^22 log^3 m) (derived, not in the paper). All l-bit strings are valid pointers since m=2^l, so no invalid-pointer case arises.

def-transcript.first_lean_target: structure BoolCircuit (nIn nOut) with gates in topological order, each of fan-in <= 2, and outputs d,b among the non-input gates; def Transcript C := Fin C.size -> Bool; def gateOK C x t g : Prop.

prop-3.3.proof_notes: Reader audit. Cost is O_k(sqrt m (log m)^4), so b=4 with a k-dependent constant also works. The worst-case cap covers every branch. No property of the Forrelation promise is used beyond lem-2.1.ii and lem-2.1.iii.
